title: Finite normal field envelope retaining a semilinear finite group
statement:
Let $K\subseteq L$ be a finite extension of fields [def-weil-field, def-pc-field-extension, def-pc-field-tower], let $H$ be a finite group, and let $A:H\to\operatorname{Aut}(K)$ be a group homomorphism, not necessarily injective. Put $F=K^H=\{x\in K:A_h(x)=x\text{ for all }h\in H\}$. There is a tower $F\subseteq K\subseteq L\subseteq M$ with $M/F$ finite and normal. For this tower define the group
$$J=\{(h,\sigma)\in H\times\operatorname{Aut}_F(M):\sigma|_K=A_h\},\qquad \rho:J\to H,\quad (h,\sigma)\mapsto h,$$
with componentwise multiplication. Then $J$ is finite, $\rho$ is surjective, and $J$ acts on $M$ by $(h,\sigma)\cdot m=\sigma(m)$, compatibly with $A$ on $K$. If $N=\ker\rho$, the map $\operatorname{Aut}_K(M)\to N$, $\sigma\mapsto(1,\sigma)$ is a group isomorphism compatible with the actions on $M$, and $M^N/K$ is finite purely inseparable. Also $K/F$ is finite Galois and $M/K$ is finite normal. If $L/K$ is separable, the same witnesses can be chosen with $M/F$ finite Galois; then $M/K$ is finite Galois and $M^N=K$.

Normal means that every element's minimal polynomial over the base splits in the larger field. Separable has the meaning of [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]; finite Galois means finite, normal and separable. Purely inseparable has the meaning of [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension]. A fixed field is the subfield of elements fixed by every indicated automorphism.

source.place: Agent combination of Tag 09I3 lemma-galois-over-fixed-field, Tag 09DT lemma-normal-closure, Tag 0EXM lemma-normal-closure-galois, Tag 0BME lemma-lift-maps (2), and Tag 030M lemma-normal-case; compatible-pair group retaining the original H.

proof.text: Put $H_0=A(H)\subseteq\operatorname{Aut}(K)$. It is a finite group, since it is an image of $H$, and its inclusion acts faithfully on $K$. An element is fixed by $H_0$ exactly when it is fixed by every $A_h$, so $K^{H_0}=F$. Apply [lem-wf-finite-field-action-fixed-degree] to this faithful action. It gives that $K/F$ is finite, separable and normal. Each $A_h$ fixes $F$ pointwise and is an $F$-automorphism of $K$.

source.place: Tag 09I3, lemma-galois-over-fixed-field; reduction of a nonfaithful action to its image.

proof.text: Choose finite spanning sets $b_i$ for $K/F$ and $c_j$ for $L/K$. Writing $x=\sum_j k_jc_j$ and $k_j=\sum_i f_{ij}b_i$ shows that the finitely many products $b_ic_j$ span $L/F$. Thus $L/F$ is finite. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-extension-in-finite-normal-extension] to $L/F$ to obtain $M/L$ with $M/F$ finite and normal. Use this tower $F\subseteq K\subseteq L\subseteq M$ for the general-case construction.

source.place: Tag 09DT, lemma-normal-closure, existence; spanning-set argument as in Tag 09G9, lemma-multiplicativity-degrees.

proof.text: Inside $H\times\operatorname{Aut}_F(M)$ take the subset $J$ in the statement. It contains $(1,1)$. For $(h,\sigma),(g,\tau)\in J$ and $k\in K$, $(\sigma\tau)(k)=\sigma(A_g(k))=A_h(A_g(k))=A_{hg}(k)$. Also $\sigma^{-1}(k)=A_{h^{-1}}(k)$, by applying $\sigma^{-1}$ to $\sigma(A_{h^{-1}}(k))=k$. Hence $J$ is closed under products and inverses and inherits the componentwise group law. Its first projection is the homomorphism $\rho$. Its second projection acts by field automorphisms: $(jj')\cdot m=j\cdot(j'\cdot m)$ and $1\cdot m=m$ follow from composition. For $j=(h,\sigma)$ and $k\in K$, $j\cdot k=A_h(k)$ proves compatibility.

source.place: Agent compatible-pair construction; elementary subgroup and action calculation.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-extension-finitely-many-embeddings] with base $F$, domain $M$ and codomain $M$. The set of $F$-algebra maps $M\to M$ is finite. Forgetting the inverse injects $\operatorname{Aut}_F(M)$ into this set. Therefore this group is finite, as are $H\times\operatorname{Aut}_F(M)$ and its subset $J$.

source.place: Tag 09H8, lemma-count-embeddings-explicitly; finite embedding-count bound in the cited node.

proof.text: Fix $h\in H$. Both $K/F$ and $M/F$ are normal by steps 1 and 2. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-normal-subextension-automorphism-extends] with $k=F$, intermediate field $K$, ambient field $M$ and automorphism $A_h$. It gives $\sigma\in\operatorname{Aut}_F(M)$ with $\sigma|_K=A_h$. Thus $(h,\sigma)\in J$ maps to $h$, proving $\rho$ surjective. No homomorphic choice of lifts is needed.

source.place: Tag 0BME, lemma-lift-maps (2); intermediate field is normal here as required by the cited specialization.

proof.text: An element of $N=\ker\rho$ is exactly a pair $(1,\sigma)$ with $\sigma|_K=A_1=1$. Such a $\sigma$ is a $K$-automorphism of $M$; conversely, every $K$-automorphism fixes $F\subseteq K$ and supplies such a pair. Hence $\sigma\mapsto(1,\sigma)$ and $(1,\sigma)\mapsto\sigma$ are mutually inverse homomorphisms between $\operatorname{Aut}_K(M)$ and $N$. Their actions both evaluate to $\sigma(m)$ on $m\in M$, so their fixed fields coincide and contain $K$.

source.place: Agent compatible-pair construction; elementary kernel and action identification.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-normal-extension-normal-over-intermediate] to $F\subseteq K\subseteq M$ to obtain that $M/K$ is algebraic and normal. A finite $F$-spanning set of $M$ also spans over $K$, so $M/K$ is finite. By [lem-weil-pbc-normal-extension-fixed-field-purely-inseparable] its fixed field under $\operatorname{Aut}_K(M)$ is purely inseparable over $K$. Step 6 identifies this field with $M^N$. It is finite over $K$: a $K$-linearly independent subset of the subspace $M^N\subseteq M$ is linearly independent in $M$, so has cardinality at most $\dim_K M$.

source.place: Tag 09HN, lemma-normal-goes-up; Tag 030M, lemma-normal-case (2) and its fixed-field identification; elementary subspace dimension bound.

proof.text: Assume $L/K$ is separable. Since $K/F$ is separable by step 1, [lem-zl-separable-permanence] gives that $L/F$ is separable. Its finiteness was established in step 2 before choosing $M$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-galois-receiving-separable-extensions] to the singleton family $L/F$. It gives a finite Galois extension $M/F$ and an $F$-embedding $L\hookrightarrow M$. Identify $L$ with its image and use the induced copies of $K$ and $F$, obtaining a tower extending the specified $F\subseteq K\subseteq L$. Use this $M$ in steps 3--7, whose construction only required finiteness and normality over $F$.

source.place: Tag 09HB, lemma-separable-permanence; Tags 09DT, lemma-normal-closure and 0EXM, lemma-normal-closure-galois, in the singleton specialization of the cited node.

proof.text: For the witnesses of step 8, [lem-sfb-separable-algebraic-intermediate-base] applied to $F\subseteq K\subseteq M$ makes $M/K$ separable. Together with step 7 this makes $M/K$ finite Galois. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-galois-fixed-field] to $M/K$: the elements fixed by every $K$-automorphism are exactly $K$. The action-compatible identification in step 6 therefore gives $M^N=K$.

source.place: Tag 09H2, lemma-separable-goes-up (2); Tag 09DW, theorem-galois-theory, fixed-field clause.

(3) The subgroup and action follow from (στ)|_K=A_hA_g and σ^{-1}|_K=A_{h^{-1}}. (4) The embedding bound gives Aut_F(M) finite. (5) 0BME(2) needs K/F normal, which holds by step 1 (I read fields.tex 1946ff), so ρ is onto. (6) N equals Aut_K(M). (9) 09H2 with 09DW gives M^N=K. Small cases agree with the statement: H trivial, A trivial, and in char p M=K(a^{1/p}) gives M^N=M, which is purely inseparable but not equal to K, as the general clause says.
